thesis: Block runs two linked networks — Square for merchants and Cash App for consumers — and is converting scale into margin faster than the market has repriced. Q2 2026 gross profit rose 25% to $3.17B with a record 27% adjusted operating margin and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.02 (+65%), and FY2026 guidance was raised to $12.51B of gross profit (+21%), $3.47B of adjusted operating income and $4.02 of adjusted diluted EPS (+70%). At $73.31 the stock is ~18x guided adjusted EPS and ~12x $3.88B of TTM free cash flow with roughly zero net debt, versus a $95–$98 street consensus target. The bet is that the February 2026 restructuring (~4,000 roles cut, workforce targeted below 6,000) holds while Cash App lending keeps compounding above 40%; the primary risk is consumer credit deterioration hitting that lending book first and hardest.

drivers: Gross profit growth holds near 20% into FY2027 and FY2027 adjusted EPS reaches ~$5.50, supporting ~20x
February 2026 AI restructuring savings land in full and adjusted operating margin pushes past 30%
Cash App lending (Borrow plus Afterpay) scales further without a credit break, keeping Financial Solutions gross profit above 40% growth
Square and Cash App cross-pollination (local merchant discovery, Cash App as tender at Square sellers) turns two networks into one flywheel
Bitcoin recovery revives the Bitcoin Ecosystem line and turns the 9,032 BTC treasury into a tailwind for reported GAAP earnings

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 guidance is met ($12.51B gross profit, $4.02 adjusted diluted EPS), FY2027 gross profit grows mid-to-high teens, FY2027 adjusted EPS lands near $5.20, and the multiple holds at 17–18x. Consumer credit normalises without a spike in loss rates and the headcount reduction is margin-accretive without visibly slowing product velocity. This is roughly where the 42–46 analyst consensus target of $95–$98 sits.

risks: Consumer credit deteriorates and Cash App Borrow / Afterpay loan-loss provisions absorb the 2026 margin gains
The ~40% headcount reduction damages product velocity and gross profit growth decelerates two to four quarters out
Square GPV growth slows into single digits under pressure from Toast, Shopify, Clover, Stripe and Adyen
Multiple compresses to 11–12x on flat ~$4.30 adjusted EPS, with the $48.21 fifty-two-week low as reference floor
Continued bitcoin weakness keeps GAAP net income depressed (TTM $357M vs $1.31B in FY2025) and deters generalist buyers

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (expected) — guided to 18% gross profit growth and ~89% adjusted diluted EPS growth; first clean read on restructuring savings
Realisation of February 2026 AI restructuring savings and progress toward the 28% full-year adjusted operating margin guide
Q4 and FY2026 results with initial FY2027 guidance — the key test of whether ~20% gross profit growth is sustainable
Cash App lending credit performance through the consumer cycle; Square Financial Services balance-sheet expansion retaining more lending economics
Bitcoin price trajectory — drives Bitcoin Ecosystem revenue and fair-value marks on the 9,032 BTC treasury, and therefore reported GAAP earnings

key_risks: Consumer credit cycle exposure through Cash App Borrow and the Afterpay BNPL book
Execution risk on the February 2026 restructuring (~4,000 roles cut, AI agents substituted for internal work)
GAAP earnings volatility from fair-value accounting on the bitcoin treasury (TTM GAAP net income $357M vs $1.31B FY2025)
Competitive pressure on Square from Toast, Shopify, Clover, Stripe and Adyen
Regulatory and compliance overhang, including federal scrutiny of AML and consumer-compliance programmes (status unverified)
Bitcoin Ecosystem revenue decline (-12.8% YoY) depressing headline growth optics
Near-term sentiment drag from insider selling and a stock below its 50-day moving average
